label: Agile Regulatory Delivery Pattern
description: Adapt agile delivery for fixed-deadline, fixed-scope regulatory programmes. Embed compliance gates inside sprints, write regulatory acceptance criteria, make evidence and audit trail a definition-of-done, and reconcile iterative delivery with immovable supervisory milestones (AMLR, DORA, MiCA, CSRD, EU AI Act).

claudeKnowledge.description: Scrum Guide (2020) and SAFe; Disciplined Agile; EU regulatory instruments and their compliance dates — AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 (apply 10 Jul 2027), AMLA Reg (EU) 2024/1620 (AMLA operational mid-2025, direct supervision from 2028), AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640, DORA (EU) 2022/2554 (apply 17 Jan 2025), MiCA (EU) 2023/1114, TFR (EU) 2023/1113, EU AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 (staged 2025–2027), CSRD (EU) 2022/2464 + ESRS; supervisory expectations on change management, evidence and audit trail (EBA, ESMA, national competent authorities)

guidedInputs.label: Fixed Regulatory Milestones & Dates
guidedInputs.description: List the immovable supervisory milestones, their dates, and any dependency between them. These become the backward-planning anchors.
guidedInputs.placeholder:
e.g.
- 10 Jul 2027: AMLR provisions apply (hard stop)
- Q4 2026: Board sign-off on updated BWRA required before policy rewrite
- Mar 2027: Supervisory dialogue / readiness self-assessment to FI
- 2028: AMLA direct supervision begins for selected entities

guidedInputs.label: In-Scope Delivery Workstreams
guidedInputs.description: Which compliance workstreams will be delivered iteratively under this pattern?

guidedInputs.label: Known Constraints, Risks or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe what is making fixed-deadline delivery hard: scope creep, dependency on regulator clarifications (RTS/ITS not yet final), vendor lead times, audit findings, resource gaps.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Key AMLA RTS on CDD not yet finalised, so acceptance criteria for the onboarding workstream are provisional. Vendor for transaction-monitoring has a 6-month implementation lead time. Internal Audit flagged weak change-control evidence in the last cycle. Product owner is shared across three regulatory programmes.

exampleInput: We are a Swedish payment institution running an AMLR/AMLA readiness programme that must be operational by the 10 July 2027 application date. We deliver in two-week Scrum sprints across four squads (onboarding/CDD, transaction monitoring, policy & governance, and data/reporting), but our PMO still runs a classic stage-gate over the top and Internal Audit recently flagged that our change-control evidence is thin and reconstructed after the fact. Some AMLA RTS we depend on are not yet final. Design an agile delivery pattern for this programme: how to embed compliance gates inside sprints, write regulatory acceptance criteria and a regulator-grade definition-of-done, backward-plan the sprints from the immovable supervisory milestones, and run the programme so that the audit trail is a by-product of delivery rather than a scramble at the end.

exampleValues.milestone_map: 10 Jul 2027: AMLR provisions apply (hard stop). Q4 2026: Board sign-off on refreshed business-wide risk assessment. Mar 2027: readiness self-assessment to Finansinspektionen. 2028: AMLA direct-supervision regime begins.
exampleValues.known_concerns: Several AMLA RTS we depend on are not yet final, so onboarding acceptance criteria are provisional. Transaction-monitoring vendor has a 6-month lead time. Internal Audit flagged weak, after-the-fact change-control evidence. The product owner is shared across three programmes.
